newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL AND DEPORTIVO FACE TOUGH CUP TESTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL AND DEPORTIVO FACE TOUGH CUP TESTS.

text.p: Real Madrid take a slender 2-1
advantage to Valladolid on Wednesday in the top second leg game
in the third round of the Spanish Cup.
Deportivo Coruna, third in the league, will have to turn
round a 2-0 defeat at Sevilla in the first leg, while an early
Cup exit against Racing Santander could cost the head of
Zaragoza's second manager of the season, Victor Esparrago.
Zaragoza -- who are next to last in the league less than two
seasons after taking the European Cup Winners' Cup -- managed
only a 1-1 draw in the first leg which they ended with just nine
men.
Espanyol coach Pepe Carcelen resigned on Monday, but has
left newly-named successor Vicente Miera a 4-1 first leg win
over Sporting Gijon as his Cup legacy.
Rayo Vallecano are the only top flight side in danger of
falling to opponents from lower divisions after going down 3-2
in Pamplona to Osasuna.
Real Betis' league fixture at the weekend was postponed
because of a flu bug that has hit many of their players and
which doctors think was incubated in the return trip from the
1-0 first leg victory at Granada.
Betis, fourth in the league, are still without nearly half
their first-team squad and are struggling to put together a team
for Wednesday's game.
After stunning Barcelona by coming back to win 3-2 in
Monday's league game, Hercules travel to Lleida to play a first
leg tie which was postponed because of bad weather.
